_about: Per-item and per-card notes for scripts/grammar-lab-build.js where the source text alone does not say enough, keyed by topic id. An item number holds { text } (the line to read instead: a 6-8 question with no choices given, written with its choices, or a writing item set in its short passage) or, for a run-on, { accept: [joining words] } (more valid fixes), or { title } (a book or movie title the sentence holds, shown in italics); card.sections[i].highlight lists which sentences of a writing card's worked passage are highlighted (0 is the first).

12.text: 12. "Maya said, 'I will never forget this day.'" Which context is missing when nothing else is given: "The listener and the plot clue" or "The speaker" or "Nothing, the context is complete"? Answer: "The listener and the plot clue" Hint: Good context names the speaker, the listener, and what is happening in the plot.

11.text: 11. Which is why source information matters: "It helps the reader judge whether to trust the fact." or "It makes the sentence longer." or "It tells the reader the fact is serious."? Answer: "It helps the reader judge whether to trust the fact." Hint: Knowing who said it and where it was published lets the reader check it.

7.text: 7. Which is the first step to paraphrase safely: "Read the idea, look away, and write it in your own words." or "Copy the sentence, then change one or two words." or "Read the idea, then copy its best phrases."? Answer: "Read the idea, look away, and write it in your own words." Hint: Looking away keeps you from copying the original wording.

10.text: 10. Which is why you must name the source even when you paraphrase: "The idea still belongs to someone else, so the reader needs to know where it came from." or "A paraphrase uses the same words as the original." or "Naming the source makes the paraphrase your own idea."? Answer: "The idea still belongs to someone else, so the reader needs to know where it came from." Hint: A paraphrase is not your own idea, so credit the source.

6.text: 6. Which goes inside the parentheses for a book source: "The author's last name and the page number" or "The author's full name, a comma, and the page" or "The book's title and the year"? Answer: "The author's last name and the page number" Hint: Look back at the worked examples and see what each set of parentheses holds.

12.text: 12. Which is the purpose of an in-text citation: "It shows the reader where a fact or quote came from." or "It makes a fact sound more serious." or "It replaces the period at the end of the sentence."? Answer: "It shows the reader where a fact or quote came from." Hint: A citation names the source so the reader can check it.

9.text: 9. "First, the class planned the garden." Where does a transition usually sit: "At the start of the sentence it connects, followed by a comma" or "At the start of the sentence, with no comma after it" or "At the end of the sentence, after the period"? Answer: "At the start of the sentence it connects, followed by a comma" Hint: Look back at the worked passages and notice where each transition sits and what punctuation follows it.

1.text: 1. Passage: "Schools should keep art classes. Art classes belong in every school. If we protect art classes now, the next generation of artists, builders, and thinkers will thank us." Which sentence restates the claim in fresh words? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A conclusion restates the claim in fresh words.

2.text: 2. Same passage. Which sentence leaves a final thought? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A final thought looks ahead and gives the reader a reason to care.

4.text: 4. Passage: "The town needs a new library. A new library would serve the whole town. A bigger library would open its doors to every reader in town for years to come." Which sentence restates the claim in fresh words? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A conclusion restates the claim in fresh words.

5.text: 5. Same passage. Which sentence leaves a final thought? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A final thought looks ahead and gives the reader a reason to care.

7.text: 7. Passage: "Recess should last 30 minutes. Thirty minutes of recess gives every student time to play and recharge. Longer recess would send students back to class ready to learn." Which sentence restates the claim in fresh words? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A conclusion restates the claim in fresh words.

8.text: 8. Same passage. Which sentence leaves a final thought? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A final thought gives the reader something to remember.

10.text: 10. Passage: "Every student should learn to cook. Cooking is a skill every student should carry into adult life. A student who can cook a simple meal will never go hungry." Which sentence restates the claim in fresh words? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A conclusion restates the claim in fresh words.

11.text: 11. Same passage. Which sentence leaves a final thought? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A final thought gives the reader something to remember.

12.text: 12. Which are the two jobs of a conclusion: "Restate the claim in fresh words, and leave a final thought" or "Bring in new evidence, and start a new argument" or "Repeat the essay word for word, and add a new claim"? Answer: "Restate the claim in fresh words, and leave a final thought" Hint: A conclusion reminds the reader of the main point and ends with something to remember.

1.text: 1. Passage: "School should start later. Some people say a later start would push sports and jobs into the evening. Sports can end a little later, and studies show that rested students learn more, so the trade is worth it." Which sentence is the counterargument? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A counterargument names the strongest point on the other side.

2.text: 2. Same passage. Which sentence is a good response to it? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A good response takes the concern seriously and answers it with a fact.

3.text: 3. Passage: "The town needs a new library. Some people say a new library would cost too much money. The cost would be shared over many years, and a bigger library would serve the whole town." Which sentence is the counterargument? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A counterargument names the strongest point on the other side.

4.text: 4. Same passage. Which sentence is a good response to it? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A good response takes the concern seriously and answers it with a reason.

5.text: 5. Passage: "Recess should last 30 minutes. Some people say longer recess would take time from lessons. Rested students learn faster, so the time is not lost." Which sentence is the counterargument? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A counterargument names the strongest point on the other side.

6.text: 6. Same passage. Which sentence is a good response to it? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A good response takes the concern seriously and answers it with a reason.

7.text: 7. Where does a counterargument paragraph usually go: "After the main reasons and before the conclusion" or "Before the claim, as the first paragraph" or "After the conclusion, as the last word"? Answer: "After the main reasons and before the conclusion" Hint: The writer answers the other side and then ends strong.

8.text: 8. Passage: "Every student should learn to cook. Some people say cooking lessons would take time from other classes. Cooking teaches math and science too, so the lessons do double duty." Which sentence is the counterargument? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A counterargument names the strongest point on the other side.

9.text: 9. Same passage. Which sentence is a good response to it? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A good response takes the concern seriously and answers it with a reason.

11.text: 11. Passage: "Bikes should be allowed on the river path. Some people say bikes would make the path unsafe for walkers. Marked lanes and signs would keep walkers and riders safe." Which sentence is the counterargument? Answer: the second sentence. Hint: A counterargument names the strongest point on the other side.

12.text: 12. Same passage. Which sentence is a good response to it? Answer: the third sentence. Hint: A good response takes the concern seriously and answers it with a reason.

7.text: 7. "The books were returned to the library." Which reason fits a writer choosing passive voice here: "The doer is unknown or unimportant, and the books matter most." or "The books did the returning themselves." or "Passive voice makes the doer the subject."? Answer: "The doer is unknown or unimportant, and the books matter most." Hint: Ask whether the reader needs to know who returned the books.

11.text: 11. "The deep lake was still and clear." Where are the adjectives, and what do they describe? Answer: deep, still, and clear. Hint: Look for every describing word, then ask where each one sits.

12.text: 12. "An icy path crossed the frozen pond." Where are the adjectives? Answer: icy and frozen. Hint: Look at each noun and ask which word describes it.
